To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

patients going through a total hip arthroscopy programme cope by economizing on their mental resources, being physically active, and striving to meet the expectations of the programme, in order to restore their physical, mental, and psychosical integrity.
patients going through a total hip arthroscopy programme, with the aim of restoring physical and psychosical integrity, use different types of coping to achieve their goal.
the predominant coping types are: (a) mentally proactive, (b) physically active, (c) mentally active, and (d) mentally passive.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the behavioural processes that are activated in patients when coping with a fast-track surgery programme.
the behavioural process of coping, the predominant coping types, and the coping type-specific features of patients undergoing fast track total hip replacements.
the question of how patients understand and deal with the demands of a fast track total joint arthroplasty.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the patients who were most successful in coping with a fast-track total hip arthroscopy programme had a strong motivation for rehabilitation and a high degree of self-efficacy.
patients’ main concern is to restore their physical integrity, which has been compromised by reduced mobility and function in daily life.
the patients’ predominant coping type is a combination of being mentally proactive and being physically active.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the patients’ coping behaviour is characterized by a striving for physical and psychosociological integrity.
patients going through the fast track programme cope with the programme by economizing their mental resources, being mentally proactive, and physically active.
patients going through a programme like this have to cope with a lot of things.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the fast track concept needs to be adapted to patients’ individual needs.
fast track programmes should be adapted to individual patient characteristics and needs.
patients who do not meet fast track programme expectations are not a failure, they are simply different.
